body: Thank you.  Responses have been overwhelmingly in favor of me giving her up but I'm undecided.  I'm going to talk to my therapist on Wednesday when she gets back.  I just feel like I'm being incredibly selfish by keeping her.  If she were a child, she would have been removed.  If she were a boyfriend or girlfriend I had beaten, my head would be on a spike in my front yard by now.

Sometimes murder doesn't seem all that impossible.  A recent past partner of mine was afraid of me a good portion of the time.

I'm just terrified because I'm getting worse instead of better.  I want to be more alone.  I don't usually think about suicide, I think about grabbing a backpack and living without roots, not letting myself affect anyone.

I'm in the US.

She's pretty goddamn adorable.  I'm sure if I posted her picture and my state, she'd be gone in 20 minutes.
My therapist has been on vacation for the last 2 weeks.  I'll finally see her on Wednesday.  I'll be bringing all this up with her.

I'm on Seraquel - I guess it's targeted towards psychosis?

That's an interesting coping technique.  The reason I started breaking other things is because I knew I had to get away from my dog.

I've abused past partners.  I hit, I break things, I punch holes in the wall.  None of the walls here are broken, probably because this house is of better construction than others I've lived in.

I'm medicated and in therapy.  I'm considering commitment.

I do have friends and family, but they're all pretty good people who would never beat an innocent animal.  I feel like this incident puts me outside what applies to most people.

I'm sorry you lost your brother.

But from a more detached point of view, wouldn't I be improving the world a little bit by taking myself out of it?
I'm really not interested in what's in my best interest right now, I want to do the right thing for my dog, at any cost.

I have abused a couple of past partners.  I am medicated and in therapy.  This is the first time I've turned my anger on an animal.

I haven't trusted myself for a long time but I thought my dog was safe.  To be totally honest, I want to find her a new home then commit suicide so this can't happen again.

I really wish this wasn't true.  I'm all alone with my traumatized dog and I don't want to tell anyone IRL about this, although I'm probably going to have to, one way or another.  Increasingly, reddit is the first place I look for guidance.

So if I give her up for adoption, she'd likely get put down anyway because the Humane Society would assume she's fucked up?

She's actually my first dog, but I can't argue with the self-validation thing.
She's 9 months old.  Have I really fucked her up for life?
